chunks: A number of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from Abī Wahb, from Muḥammad ibn Manṣūr, who said:
I asked him عليه السلام about the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic:

And when they commit an immorality, they say: We found our fathers upon it, and Allah has commanded us to it. Say: Surely Allah does not command indecency. Do you say about Allah what you do not know?

He said: So he عليه السلام said: Have you ever seen anyone who claimed that Allah commanded adultery, drinking wine, or anything from these prohibitions? So I said: No. He عليه السلام said: Then what is this immorality which they claim Allah commanded them with? I said: Allah and His Guardian know best.

He عليه السلام said: This concerns the Imams of tyranny: they claimed that Allah commanded the people to follow a people whom Allah had not commanded them to follow. So Allah refuted that against them, informed that they had spoken a lie against Him, and named that from them an immorality.

key_terms.أَئِمَّةِ الْجَوْرِ: leaders of tyranny who unjustly claim authority
key_terms.الِائْتِمَامِ: following or taking someone as an Imam
key_terms.الْفَحْشَاءِ: indecency or immorality, which Allah does not command
key_terms.فَاحِشَةً: a grave indecency or outrageous wrongdoing; here, falsely attributing illegitimate authority to Allah
key_terms.وَلِيُّهُ: His Guardian, referring to the divinely authorized wali

ai.seo_question: How do Shia hadith interpret Qur'an 7:28 regarding immorality and false claims about Allah?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the verse as referring not to people openly claiming that Allah commands acts like adultery or drinking wine, but to false leaders who attribute illegitimate religious authority to Allah. The Imam عليه السلام interprets the 'immorality' here as the grave falsehood of claiming divinely sanctioned leadership for those whom Allah did not appoint.
